name: Suprematism
visualIdentity: Supplemental design reference, not a directly named source-collection style. A few flat squares, circles, crosses, and bars sit in an open field; size, angle, balance, and negative space carry the composition. Keep forms abstract and free of illustrative textures.
suitableUses: Explicit fits include motion posters and staged geometric compositions; product, editorial, UI, and explanatory storytelling may suit it when sparse geometry supports the subject. Inference: use it for exhibition titles or minimal artistic statements when the open, abstract treatment serves the message.
limitations: Sparse forms and open space are central. Avoid dense layouts, illustrative textures, or narrative recomposition that obscures hierarchy or adds no explanatory value. For the suggested title hybrid, limit copy to five words, avoid paragraphs and fast kinetic sequences, and keep words readable.
palette: Suggested tokens for new artwork only: white #FFFFFF background, black #000000 foreground, red #C92B2B, yellow #E8BE30, and blue #2453A0 accents. Keep the restricted primary and black/white family, discrete flat fields, and no gradients. Task, brand, approved palette, semantic roles, and asset colors take precedence; never auto-recolor or expand hues. Check actual text contrast after compositing.
motionAndInteraction: Video: slowly shift position, rotation, and proportion while preserving negative space and visual center of gravity. Use deterministic, seekable time; avoid generic bounce or smoothing. Optional narrative patterns include a pinned-stage internal recomposition, reversible chapter handoff, or story steps with reading holds, only when supported by content. Interactive HTML may map finite scroll progress to states, pin a defined outer stage while inner forms move, then release without a jump; support backward motion and reduced-motion/static states.
audio: Unspecified by the style. Choose music, voiceover, effects, ambience, or silence for the topic and audience; honor supplied audio choices, avoid competing with speech or reading, and synchronize to visual cadence. Do not assume assets exist.
assetRequirements: Flat SVG shapes are the primary suggested renderer; Canvas 2D is an alternative. Use few geometric forms and any exact approved copy or palette supplied by the task. Text in the optional title hybrid should be real, readable text. Other asset requirements are unspecified.
combinations: Usually strongest alone. The explicit suggested hybrid is style-093 sparse title words used as weighted bars: one or two words may drift and rotate slowly among geometric forms. Preserve readability, use black or one primary token, and avoid textures. Use only if words must become part of the composition.
productionApproach: Choose renderer and motion engine for visual fidelity first; SVG plus GSAP is the suggested route. HyperFrames handles composition, seekable timing, media/audio sync, checks, and export; Remotion is only a documented fallback if HyperFrames is unavailable or verified insufficient. Keep one owner per animated property. For HTML, adapt scroll interactions separately from video timing; validate direct, reverse, and sequential states.
